title: Referenced integral diagonal coefficient family
statement: For every prime ell and separated finite-type scheme Y over a field of positive characteristic different from ell, there is a diagonal coefficient Family whose completed class and all three traces have a Reference. Localization-size choices and the completed arrow are retained existentially; no arbitrary data are defined from existence.

source.place: Paragraph (1), diagonal unit, trace counit and the two triangle identities

proof.text: The characteristic assumption makes ell nonzero in k; map its unit along k -> Gamma(Y, top). Finite type over Spec(k), then the projective-line morphism and its base change, give Noetherianity of Y, P1_Y and its self-square. Construct the localization choices: pro-etale abelian and module sheaves are Grothendieck, as are completed module sheaves by the coefficient-universe theorem. Countable functor categories inherit filtered exact colimits and a separator constructed from the evaluation left adjoints applied to a separator of the coefficient category. K-injective resolutions and local smallness give the derived localizations in universe u+1; Grothendieck abelianity also supplies Ext in that universe. These are constructed choices, retained existentially in the conclusion.
Apply exists_diagonalTowerSystem with the constructed unit and localization choices to obtain D, its completion specification and its normalized strict cycle system.

Apply diagonalTower_limit with p=ringChar(k) to D. Retain its nine data witnesses, finite Cartier normalization and ordinary cone comparisons. The proved private selectEquation helper selects the uniquely specified completed arrow and its equation. The proved private selectPresentation helper returns the existential completed arrow directly, retaining the original compatibility predicate and grouping it with both cone normalizations before adjoining the selected equation. The private selectDiagonalLimit helper first unfolds DiagonalCompletedLimitSpec and the four irreducible normalization predicates, then applies this conversion before specializing localization choices. The resulting presentation is exactly IsDiagonalLimit, including its original compatibility witness and selected arrow equation. No uniqueness from individual finite reductions is asserted.

Apply diagonalTower_coefficients to this same D and delta with the normalized limit characterization. Keep its Family and Reference, and package them with the same unit proof and all three localization choices as IntegralFamilyReference. No choice of a Family is made in a definition, and no uniqueness from individual reductions is asserted.

lean.statement:
theorem integralNormalizedFamily_exists
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ℓ)]
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] :
    ∃ family : Family ℓ Y, IntegralFamilyReference ℓ Y family
